status_vocabulary.source-reported: A named source states the claim; the Commons has not independently established it.
status_vocabulary.primary-source-defined: The claim records the wording or structure of an authoritative problem/standard source.
status_vocabulary.derived-unreviewed: A derivation is public and reproducible but has not yet received independent domain review.
status_vocabulary.independently-reproduced: An independent contributor reproduced the stated artifact/result within the recorded scope.
status_vocabulary.independently-reviewed: A qualified independent reviewer accepted the stated claim within the recorded scope.
status_vocabulary.disputed: A material unresolved objection is recorded.
status_vocabulary.superseded: A later record replaces this one without deleting history.

claims.statement: OpenAI published an analytic Navier-Stokes proof and a Lean formalization on 2026-09-08.
OpenAI states that its result establishes alternatives C and D of the official Clay formulation.
The official Clay Navier-Stokes problem formulation contains alternatives A, B, C and D, and the C/D alternatives permit a smooth external force.
The public Observatory represents leading-order inner-core scaling relations from Section 2.1 of the cited OpenAI paper and does not purport to reconstruct the full velocity field.
Under the recorded normalized scaling model, the core energy scale is proportional to tau^(1/2-3h) while the angular speed scale is proportional to tau^(-1/2-h), for 0 < h < 1/100.
